text:
Eloise - Sales: Quick sync - Acme wants a 2-week Dedicated POC. Blocking item: their security only allows outbound to rotating IPs (rotates every 24h). They asked if we can consume a list that changes daily or if they need a static egress.
Jorge (netops): We can support three practical flows: 1) customer exposes a stable egress (EIP) or NAT/proxy -> easiest; 2) customer provides a CIDR range we allowlist -> requires range, not single ephemeral IPs; 3) they submit rotated IPs and we manually add them via support tickets (manual ops). We don't have a per-customer API to dynamically ingest ephemeral IPs today.
Darren (solutions): For the POC I'd recommend option 1: customer deploys a tiny NAT proxy in their cloud with a stable public IP and forwards traffic. Minimal infra and no product changes. If they need TLS inspection, advise them to avoid terminating TLS at proxy.
Mina (security): Security checklist to include in the SQA: project-scoped API key (rotate every 24h if they insist), optional IP allowlist, request/response logging, and network egress constraints. We can also offer client cert authentication but that requires our enterprise enablement and a short security review.
Eloise - Sales: Can we bind a scoped API key to a Dedicated pool so leaked keys are low blast radius?
Jorge (netops): Yes — we can create a project-scoped key and scope it to the Dedicated pool. Key will only be valid for calls routed to that pool. For quick testing you can generate a hosted key and restrict by source IP on our side.
Darren (solutions): Example test curl from their bastion (replace KEY and HOST):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer ${POC_KEY}" \
  https://dedicated-us-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"test"}'
```
Make sure the proxy egress IP is on the allowlist. If the proxy does TLS termination, SNI allowlisting may not work reliably.
Mina (security): Note: Our Dedicated endpoints currently accept IPv4 allowlists only. If the customer egress is IPv6-only, they must provide NAT64 or a dual-stack proxy.
Eloise - Sales: They asked if we can do same-day add/remove for rotating IPs via support ticket. What's realistic SLA?
Jorge (netops): We can manually add/remove entries same-day during business hours, target 2 hours from ticket acknowledgement. If they rotate outside business hours it's likely next-business-window. Manual ops scales poorly; recommend proxy with stable EIP.
Darren (solutions): For automation-minded customers we can recommend a tiny Lambda that updates their proxy EIP on rotation and posts the new EIP to us via a ticket template. Not ideal but reduces friction.
BillingBot: [quote] POC trial pricing applied: 200 hours discounted, start date tentative.
Eloise - Sales: Great. Action list: 1) I will ask customer to spin up a proxy EIP or provide a CIDR. 2) Jorge to confirm manual add/remove SLA and runbook. 3) Mina to prepare SQA blurb about keys, IP allowlist, and mTLS notes. 4) Darren to share the sample key rotation snippet. Aim: first test request within 24h. :rocket:
Jorge (netops): I'll post the runbook link and the ticket template into this thread. We will accept the manual IP via support ticket until product self-serve is available.
Mina (security): For the SQA answer use this phrasing: "POC deployments: project-scoped keys, optional IP allowlist, audit logs enabled. mTLS and client certs available for enterprise Dedicated/Private with a security review."
Darren (solutions): I'll paste the short key-rotate snippet in-channel and a troubleshooting checklist (DNS, TLS, SNI, proxy NAT) in next message.
Eloise - Sales: Thanks everyone 44d I'll loop in Acme and tie the ticket to their POC.
Jorge (netops): One more note 1: if the customer cannot provide IPv4 egress we can't add them to the allowlist today.
